entities.name: TIM-3
observations: Recipient T-cell TIM-3 signaling protected syngeneic mouse orthotopic liver grafts after 20 hours of cold storage; anti-TIM-3 worsened ALT, histology, Th1/Th17 responses, and innate-cell infiltration.
TIM-3 signaling was associated with lower T-bet/IFN-gamma, higher GATA3 and IL-4/IL-10, exhaustion markers PD-1/LAG-3, and CD4+ T-cell apoptosis in direct OLT studies.

entities.name: Galectin-9
observations: Ischemia-stressed hepatocytes were identified as a major source and releaser of galectin-9 in mouse liver grafts; recombinant galectin-9 enhanced graft resistance and was hepatoprotective in direct OLT experiments.
Combined TIM-3/Gal-9 pathway disruption worsened inflammatory responses in mouse warm hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury, which is mechanistic corroboration but not transplant evidence.

entities.name: Liver transplant IRI
observations: In syngeneic mouse orthotopic liver transplantation after 20 hours of cold storage, recipient TIM-3 enhancement reduced serum ALT and Suzuki histology injury, whereas TIM-3 blockade increased injury.

entities.name: TIM-3-Gal-9 OLT protection
observations: Direct mouse OLT evidence supports a protective recipient T-cell TIM-3/hepatocyte galectin-9 axis against cold ischemia-reperfusion injury.
The studies strongly support a functional protective axis but do not establish hepatocyte-specific galectin-9 necessity using donor hepatocyte-specific genetic loss-of-function.

entities.name: TIM-3 warm liver IRI
observations: In mouse warm partial-liver ischemia-reperfusion without transplantation, anti-TIM-3 worsened injury and inflammation; this supports the direction of effect but is not direct OLT evidence.

entities.name: TIM-3-CC1 OLT protection
observations: A 2023 mouse OLT study found related T-cell TIM-3 protection involving CEACAM1/CC1 and Kupffer-cell NF-kB, but it did not specifically test galectin-9.
